=== README.md ===
0001: # Do Again
0002: 
0003: [![CI](https://github.com/Tran-Steven/do-again/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Tran-Steven/do-again/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
0004: [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/do-again.svg?cacheSeconds=300)](https://pypi.org/project/do-again/)
0005: [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/do-again.svg?cacheSeconds=300)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/do-again)
0006: [![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/do-again.svg?cacheSeconds=300)](https://pypi.org/project/do-again/)
0007: [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Tran-Steven/do-again.svg?cacheSeconds=300)](LICENSE)
0008: 
0009: Do Again gives AI coding agents a policy-controlled way to execute work on a local development machine, return auditable receipts and artifacts, and keep iterating when another pass is needed.
0010: 
0011: ## How it works
0012: 
0013: ```text
0014: agent
0015:   |
0016:   | request
0017:   v
0018: operator-control branch
0019:   |
0020:   v
0021: Do Again -> policy validation -> local command / file / test / git action
0022:   ^                                         |
0023:   |                                         |
0024:   +----------- receipt / artifact -----------+
0025: ```
0026: 
0027: The agent can inspect the result, decide what still needs work, and submit another scoped action instead of stopping at the first attempt.
0028: 
0029: ## Install
0030: 
0031: ### Python / PyPI
0032: 
0033: ```bash
0034: pip install do-again
0035: ```
0036: 
0037: ### Node / npm
0038: 
0039: ```bash
0040: npm install -g do-again
0041: ```
0042: 
0043: or run it without a global install:
0044: 
0045: ```bash
0046: npx do-again setup
0047: ```
0048: 
0049: Both distributions expose the same command:
0050: 
0051: ```bash
0052: do-again
0053: ```
0054: 
0055: The npm package ships the same Python runtime from this repository behind a small Node launcher. It requires Node.js 18+ and Python 3.11+.
0056: 
0057: ## Quick start
0058: 
0059: From the Git repository you want an agent to work on:
0060: 
0061: ```bash
0062: pip install do-again
0063: cd my-project
0064: do-again setup
0065: do-again start
0066: do-again status
0067: ```
0068: 
0069: On the first browser-enabled setup, Do Again creates a dedicated automation Chrome/Chromium profile and opens it visibly so you can sign into ChatGPT and complete any human verification. Do Again watches for the real composer and continues automatically when sign-in is complete; you do not need to return to the terminal and confirm it. Do Again does not ask for or store your ChatGPT username or password.
0070: 
0071: After that one-time authentication step, setup automatically:
0072: 
0073: - verifies the real ChatGPT composer through CDP;
0074: - tests the saved session with Chrome's current `--headless=new` mode;
0075: - uses true headless mode when it is reliable, otherwise falls back to a real background Chrome instance;
0076: - creates and binds a dedicated automation conversation for the project;
0077: - creates the Git control branch and project policy;
0078: - installs the native user-level background service; and
0079: - verifies the local runtime.
0080: 
0081: Normal use is intentionally small:
0082: 
0083: ```bash
0084: do-again start
0085: do-again status
0086: do-again stop
0087: do-again list
0088: ```
0089: 
0090: `setup` already starts the project, so `start` is mainly for bringing it back later. Multiple projects can run at the same time; they share one dedicated authenticated browser runtime while keeping separate project conversations, service state, control worktrees, policies, and receipt queues.
0091: 
0092: If you do not want ChatGPT browser automation for a project:
0093: 
0094: ```bash
0095: do-again setup --no-browser
0096: ```
0097: 
0098: For attended use without installing a native background service:
0099: 
0100: ```bash
0101: do-again setup --no-service
0102: do-again run
0103: ```
0104: 
0105: ## Browser runtime
0106: 
0107: The browser is an implementation detail during normal operation. Do Again never attaches to your everyday Chrome/Chromium profile and does not touch your normal tabs, cookies, extensions, Firefox session, or browser history.
0108: 
0109: The shared automation profile lives under `~/.do_again/browser/profile` by default. CDP listens only on loopback, and Do Again chooses another local port if its preferred port is occupied.
0110: 
0111: The default browser mode is `auto`:
0112: 
0113: 1. first authentication is visible and interactive;
0114: 2. Do Again restarts the same persistent profile with `--headless=new`;
0115: 3. if the authenticated ChatGPT session is not reliable in true headless mode, it automatically falls back to a real Chrome process running without a startup window;
0116: 4. later starts reuse the verified mode without opening a foreground window.
0117: 
0118: The daemon monitors the browser and restarts it after crashes. Browser delivery uses a durable per-project outbox, so a receipt is retried after browser/network failures instead of being lost. Receipt markers make retries idempotent. If ChatGPT reports that a conversation reached its maximum length, Do Again creates a fresh background conversation, carries over recent conversation excerpts, bootstraps it from the Git control state, rebinds the project, and continues there.
0119: 
0120: If headless authentication fails, Do Again first checks the background browser with the same profile. If both modes fail, Do Again reports `auth_required` and waits for interactive setup. It does not repeatedly launch browsers or bypass verification. Local request execution continues, and browser receipts stay queued. Re-run `do-again setup` to reopen only the dedicated automation profile for human interaction.
0121: 
0122: Advanced/debug controls remain available when needed:
0123: 
0124: ```bash
0125: do-again browser status
0126: do-again browser test
0127: do-again browser login
0128: do-again browser stop
0129: ```
0130: 
0131: You can force a browser mode during setup with `--browser-mode headless` or `--browser-mode background`; `auto` is recommended.
0132: 
0133: ## Service lifecycle
0134: 
0135: Do Again installs a per-repository background agent using the native user-level service manager:
0136: 
0137: ```bash
0138: do-again start
0139: do-again status
0140: do-again restart
0141: do-again stop
0142: ```
0143: 
0144: Low-level `install`, `uninstall`, `init`, and foreground `run` commands remain available for advanced use and backward compatibility, but they are intentionally omitted from the primary help surface.
0145: 
0146: Each repository gets an isolated runtime, control worktree, state directory, policy copy, and service label under `~/.do_again`. The installed service runs from a copied runtime so installs made through either PyPI or npm remain stable after the invoking shell exits. `do-again init` also creates `do-again-policy.json` for project-specific operation, binary, root, timeout, and execution controls. The control branch must be dedicated and cannot be `main`, `master`, `trunk`, or the currently checked-out branch.
0147: 
0148: ## Why Do Again
0149: 
0150: - Explicit policy-based command permissions
0151: - GitHub-backed request and receipt transport
0152: - Project-scoped filesystem and command access
0153: - Deterministic audit trail and recovery
0154: - No agent API keys embedded in the project
0155: - Dedicated ChatGPT browser profile with headless-first operation
0156: - Durable retry/recovery when the browser crashes or a send fails
0157: - One shared browser runtime for multiple concurrent projects
0158: - A shared platform interface for macOS, Linux, and Windows
0159: - CI-tested on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 across all three platforms
0160: 
0161: ## Platform status
0162: 
0163: | Platform | Service backend | Browser runtime |
0164: | --- | --- | --- |
0165: | macOS | launchd | Chrome/Chromium CDP, headless-first |
0166: | Linux | systemd user service | Chrome/Chromium CDP, headless-first |
0167: | Windows | per-user Task Scheduler | Chrome/Chromium CDP, headless-first |
0168: 
0169: Do Again is currently alpha software. The foreground runner, per-repository service lifecycle, browser discovery, persistent profile model, and CDP runtime are implemented behind the same interface on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Browser availability still depends on a compatible local Chrome/Chromium installation and ChatGPT authentication.
0170: 
0171: ## Development
0172: 
0173: ```bash
0174: git clone https://github.com/Tran-Steven/do-again.git
0175: cd do-again
0176: python -m pip install .
0177: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
0178: python tools/browser_smoke.py
0179: do-again doctor
0180: ```
0181: 
0182: Disposable-profile smoke tests verify real Chrome CDP, profile persistence, and crash recovery without signing into ChatGPT. Authenticated ChatGPT round trips are a separate manual integration check; mocked tests cannot establish that a real session works in headless mode. Linux background Chrome requires a graphical session or virtual display.
0183: 
0184: ## Release model
0185: 
0186: Releases use semantic versioning. Pushing a version tag validates the shared release version, publishes the Python distribution to PyPI and the Node launcher to npm through Trusted Publishing, and creates the matching GitHub Release.
0187: 
0188: PyPI distribution name: `do-again`
0189: 
0190: npm package name: `do-again`
0191: 
0192: CLI command: `do-again`
0193: 
0194: Python package: `do_again`
0195: 
0196: ## Security
0197: 
0198: Do Again is designed around explicit allowlists, scoped filesystem roots, bounded execution, and auditable request/receipt records. Browser cookies and session data remain in the dedicated local automation profile; credentials are never requested or stored by Do Again, and CDP is bound to localhost. It should not be configured as unrestricted shell access.
0199:

=== ROADMAP.md ===
0001: # Do Again Roadmap
0002: 
0003: Do Again should be easy on the first run and still expose lower-level controls for advanced users.
0004: 
0005: ## P0 — reliable core
0006: 
0007: - [x] One-command local onboarding with `do-again setup`
0008: - [x] Project-specific policy file created by `do-again init` / `setup`
0009: - [x] Safe dedicated control-branch validation
0010: - [x] Custom Git remote support
0011: - [x] Future-dated request rejection
0012: - [x] Request-ID collision detection
0013: - [x] Durable local request locks
0014: - [x] Distributed Git-backed request claims
0015: - [x] Observable malformed-request records
0016: - [x] Chronological request ordering across timezone offsets
0017: - [x] macOS launchd lifecycle
0018: - [x] Linux systemd user-service lifecycle
0019: - [x] Windows per-user Task Scheduler lifecycle
0020: 
0021: ## P1 — frictionless ChatGPT connection
0022: 
0023: - [x] Dedicated persistent automation Chrome/Chromium profile
0024: - [x] One-time visible ChatGPT sign-in / human-verification flow
0025: - [x] Real composer/session verification over localhost CDP
0026: - [x] True `--headless=new` operation when the authenticated session supports it
0027: - [x] Automatic background-headed fallback when true headless is unreliable
0028: - [x] No normal-profile attachment and no post-setup foreground focus requirement
0029: - [x] Per-project automation conversation binding
0030: - [x] Shared browser runtime across concurrent projects
0031: - [x] Browser crash detection and automatic restart
0032: - [x] Durable browser-delivery outbox with idempotent receipt retries
0033: - [x] Explicit `auth_required` state instead of challenge/auth bypass loops
0034: - [x] Automatic safe new-chat rollover on conversation-length limits
0035: - [x] Browser state remains local; credentials are never requested or stored
0036: - [x] Git-backed request/receipt transport remains independent of the browser layer
0037: 
0038: ## P1 — diagnostics and recovery
0039: 
0040: - [x] Make `doctor` repository-aware and report browser/runtime repair information.
0041: - [x] Surface browser delivery failures and pending receipt count through `status`.
0042: - [ ] Surface recent core request/receipt failures without requiring users to inspect the control branch manually.
0043: - [ ] Add safe repair/reinstall behavior for damaged service definitions and runtime copies.
0044: - [ ] Add upgrade-path tests from older Do Again releases.
0045: 
0046: ## P2 — broader integration
0047: 
0048: - [ ] Pluggable transports beyond Git-backed control branches.
0049: - [ ] More end-to-end service tests on real Linux and Windows hosts, not only CI-level mocks/contracts.
0050: - [ ] Stable machine-readable CLI output for external agent integrations.
0051: - [ ] Signed release/install verification guidance.
0052: 
0053: ## 0.3.0 release validation
0054: 
0055: - [x] Unit and regression tests for shared startup, stale PID/port protection, auth recovery, rollover, and durable delivery.
0056: - [x] Real macOS Chrome smoke tests with disposable profiles, persistence, forced crash recovery, and background launch.
0057: - [x] Clean wheel, sdist, and npm installation verification.
0058: - [x] Browser hardening tests executed through a real Do Again request/receipt loop.
0059: - [x] Real Chrome smoke tests pass in Linux and Windows CI.
0060: - [x] Authenticated ChatGPT message/response succeeds after human verification and runtime restart (macOS background fallback).
0061: - [x] Publish 0.3.0 through Trusted Publishing after validation passes.
